newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks soar to record close on loan payment.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks soar to record close on loan payment.

text.p: Mexican stocks gained sharply to notch up their seventh record close in eight sessions on Wednesday in the wake of news Mexico was to prepay $5 billion on international loans, traders said.
"It really heated up at the close. The rally certainly looks like continuing apace. The number of trades and volume were overwhelming," a trader said.
The leading IPC share index .MXX ended up 96.66 points, or 2.66 percent, at 3,728.02. Volume .TV.MX was a very heavy 190.8 million shares, and an almost unheard of 7,067 trades were settled.

In the opening minutes of trade, Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz announced Mexico will pay the U.S. Treasury $3.5 billion outstanding on an emergency loan made in February 1995, and an additional $1.5 billion to the International Monetary Fund.
Market euphoria was such that Mexican shares and ADRs shunned a slump in the Dow Jones, which closed down 0.52 percent at 6,726.88 points the trader added.
"The Dow didn't even make a dent," he said.
Market heavyweight Telmex ADRs rallied 1-1/8 to 39 on Wall Street, while their L series shares in Mexico gained 80 centavos to 15.50 pesos.
Analysts said the rally was also fueled by a fortuitous combination of other economic news.

"There was a bit of everything, and all of it was good; international reserves, industrial output, exchange rate stability and falling rates were all essential for the bourse today," said Leonor Gonzlez, technical analyst at the BBV-Probursa brokerage.
On Tuesday evening, Banco de Mexico had announced its net international reserves as of Jan 10 were up to $17.863 billion, from $17.651 billion on Jan 3.
Also on Tuesday evening, the central bank assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes at 22.98 percent, a fall of 126 basis points from last week's primary auction.
Despite the sharp fall in primary rates, the benchmark 48-hour peso softened just 0.4 of a centavo to 7.8030/7.8080 per dollar.
In late trade, the Finance Ministry said November 1996 industrial production was up 11.8 percent in year-on-year terms.
Traders and analyst also drew attention to the performance by Telmex shares and ADRs.
"Telmex ADRs weakening resistance, and the pace set by their price, is very interesting. At this rate, we see their next resistance at $42.5," Gonzlez added.
"The way ADRs took off today was impressive. That shook up many quiet stocks," a trader at the Valburmex brokerage said.
Traders also noted the Inbursa brokerage made a cross trade of 20 million shares in the opening minutes of trade in Telmex, with which it has corporate links, in early trade.
"When we saw such a hefty trade in Telmex, well the rest of us did the same to get on the bandwagon," one dealer said.
On the broad market, a total of 125 stocks changed hands, of which gainers outnumbered sliders by 71 to 30.
Dealers noted the presence of construction firm Tribasa near the head of the leaders' list .PG.MX, on the back of its ADRs, they said.
Dealers said list of declining issues .PL.MX was headed by illiquid stocks after small, unrepresentative trades.

Amid the euphoria, analysts noted that whereas Mexican stocks were had closed at a record in peso terms, in dollar terms they were still well down compared to levels reached before the December 1994 devaluation crisis.

Using Reuters data, the dollar-adjusted IPC closed at 478.01 on Wednesday, compared to 672.33 on Dec 16, 1994, the last trading day before a suuden devaluation of the peso sent the Mexican economy tumbling into its worst recession in five decades.
"It is so hard to forget December 1994," one analyst said.
((--Karina Balderas, Mexico City newsroom, +525 728-7907))
